newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde June 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde June 11.

text.p: These are leading stories in afternoon daily Le Monde.

-- Germany poised to accept idea of a joint European policy against unemployment to avoid conflict with France's new socialist government which has asked for a delay before signing a stability pact limiting budget deficits of countries in a European single currency.

-- Postal services operator La Poste considers partnership with insurer AGF, offering its network of 17,000 post offices to sell casualty insurance products. The company set up for this venture would aim for a three-billion franc turnover. Project still needs to be aproved by Finance Ministry
-- Banque Rivaud placed under legal investigation for alleged fraud.

-- Luxemburg Prime Minister and Finance Minister Jean-Claude Juncker says in an interview he is relieved France remains committed to EMU, but is puzzled about the additional requests from the new French government on growth and employment.
-- Unions disappointed by appointment of expert to review alternative solutions to planned shutdown of Renault assembly plant in Vilvoorde, Belgium.
-- U.S. court orders businessman Giancarlo Parretti to pay up to 8.5 billion francs to CDR, the company set up to sell off Credit Lyonnais assets, related to loan to buy MGM studios in 1990.

-- Weight of French tax system is still driving high-technology ventures abroad, in spite of a recent pickup of venture capital investment and the creation of the Nouveau Marche for fast-growing companies.
